description: baseline

Replace the template recipe in submissions/arena/ with an airbench96-style net. Layers: frozen 2x2 patch-whitening conv (eigendecomposition computed in prepare), then three blocks of 3 convs with widths 128/384/576, BN, GELU, maxpool, then a scaled linear head with 100 outputs. Use dirac init on block convs. Train with Nesterov SGD using airbench96 lr, wd and momentum, label smoothing 0.2, Lookahead, and a linear warmup/decay schedule. Hold the full uint8 dataset on the GPU and do flip (alternating), translate 4 and cutout 12 on the GPU. Batch 1024, 8.5 epochs, bf16, channels_last, no TTA. torch.compile and warmup run in build on synthetic data; eval uses a separate path that is legal for any B. Run it twice in a row to measure the noise floor.
On the H1.1.1 recipe, change only the epoch count to 10 (schedule rescaled to match). This secures a feasible anchor and gives one point for the accuracy-vs-epoch slope.

On the best feasible airbench96 recipe, change only the compile setting: default compile becomes torch.compile(mode='max-autotune'), with CUDA-graph capture of the fixed-shape train step done in build. Handle the last partial batch by dropping it or padding it to a fixed shape. Eval stays on a separate non-graphed dynamic path; check B in {1, 7, 1024} under 5 s.
At the 8.5-epoch airbench96 recipe, change only the regularization: remove cutout and lower label smoothing from 0.2 to 0.1. Translate and flip stay as they are.

At the 8.5-epoch airbench96 recipe (which uses alternating flip), change only the flip to standard random per-image flip. This is the reverse ablation, testing whether alternating flip contributes on CIFAR-100.

On the best feasible recipe, change only the input to the whitening eigendecomposition: compute it on 5,000 randomly chosen training images (patches drawn from them) instead of all 50,000. Everything else stays fixed.
Explore: change only the widths to 128/256/384 (same 3-convs-per-block layout) and set epochs to 10 to compensate for the lower capacity. Compare it with the best feasible 128/384/576 run.

Explore. Rewrite of I009 onto the current best recipe. Start from E004 (10 epochs, no cutout). Change only the resolution schedule: for the first 50% of steps, downsample each augmented batch to 24x24 (F.interpolate, bilinear, antialias=False) after flip and translate. The remaining steps run at 32 px. Keep the LR schedule tied to step count. Compile and capture CUDA graphs for both input shapes on synthetic data in build so no recompile lands in timed train. Eval stays at 32 px.

Explore. Rewrite of I008 onto the current best recipe. Start from E004 (no cutout, LS 0.1, alternating flip, max-autotune + CUDA graph). Change only the widths, from 128/384/576 to 128/256/384 (same 3 convs per block), and set the epochs to 12 (schedule rescaled) to make up for the lower capacity. Estimated conv FLOPs per epoch are ~0.62x of the wide net.

Exploit: combine the near-miss E008 with more epochs. Start from E008, commit cd99006: E004 recipe, 50% of steps at 24 px using bilinear F.interpolate with antialias=False, both shapes compiled and CUDA-graphed in build. Change only the epoch count, from 10 to 11, with the LR schedule rescaled to the new step count so it still anneals fully. First confirm in the commit that E004 and E008 really ran 10 epochs. Timing says they did (E004 8.94 s is about E003's 10-epoch 9.01 s minus cutout), even though E004's description says 8.5.

Exploit and committee crux: on the E004 recipe (10 epochs, no cutout, LS 0.1, alternating flip, max-autotune plus CUDA graph), change only the random-translate amplitude from 4 px to 2 px. Everything else, including the epoch count, stays fixed. W4 claims translate helps, but every run so far used translate 4, so this tests whether translate 4 still over-regularizes a net that under-fits at 10 epochs, as cutout and LS 0.2 did.

Explore: narrow only the middle block. Starting from E004, change the widths from 128/384/576 to 128/256/576, keeping 3 convs per block, and set epochs to 11 with the schedule rescaled. Block 2 at 16x16 is the largest FLOP share (about 0.79 of 1.6 GMACs). Block 3's width is the likeliest source of the capacity the 100-class head needs, and E007/E009 cut both blocks. Estimated conv FLOPs per epoch are about 0.72x those of the wide net.

Mechanism test from D003 (C0029/C0031: aliasing from non-antialiased bilinear downsampling, which mismatches the 32 px-fit frozen whitening filters). On E008 (10 epochs, 50% at 24 px), change only the downsampling to F.interpolate(mode='bilinear', antialias=True), done inside the compiled and graphed step. Check in build that both shapes still capture without a recompile in timed train.

On the E004 recipe, change only the label smoothing, from 0.1 to 0.0. This tests whether the leftover smoothing still over-regularizes at 10 epochs on 100 classes, or whether its calibration benefit outweighs that.

Explore whether progress is limited by steps or by samples. On E004, change only the batch size, from 1024 to 768, at equal epochs. Under linear scaling, scale the per-step LR by 768/1024, keep wd per sample as airbench defines it, and tie the schedule to the new step count. Recapture the CUDA graph for the new shape in build and handle the last partial batch the same way as now.

One decisive test, given that C0015/C0018 contradict it. On E004, add airbench96_faster-style proxy filtering: a 32/64/64 proxy net trained alongside, scoring each 2048-image superbatch, with the main net taking an SGD step only on the top-50% by loss. Main-net epochs are counted in seen-by-main samples, and the main-net step count matches E004. Compile and graph the proxy and the main steps in build.

Exploit fallback that buys accuracy with epochs instead of regularization. Start from E013 (128/256/576, 50% of steps at 24 px with antialias, translate 4). Change only the epoch count, from 11 to 12, with the LR schedule rescaled to the new step count so it still anneals fully. This measures the per-epoch slope of the narrowed net with resize near 75%, which E010's 0.31 pp/epoch flattening left open.

Explore a gentler resolution curriculum. On E012 (128/256/576, 11 epochs, translate 4), replace the full-resolution schedule with a 24/28/32 px curriculum in thirds of steps. Downsample the augmented batch with bilinear F.interpolate (antialias=True), with the LR schedule tied to step count. Compile and CUDA-graph all three shapes on synthetic data in build, and check that no recompile lands in timed train. Compare it with E013's 50%-at-24 px (0.41 pp lost per second saved).

Explore the remaining cheap width axis. Per the FLOP accounting, after narrowing block 2, block 1 (128 ch at 32x32, ~0.45 GMACs) is about 35% of E012's conv FLOPs. On E012 (11 epochs, translate 4), change only the widths from 128/256/576 to 96/256/576, keeping 3 convs per block and the whitening output feeding block 1. E012 suggests that block-3 width carries the capacity 100 classes need, and that early-block width is cheap to cut.

Exploit the flat per-epoch slope. E010 gave 0.31 pp/epoch and E017 gave 0.11 pp/epoch near 11 epochs, so cutting epochs may be the cheapest lever left. Start from the incumbent E012 (commit 6d40ead: 128/256/576, 3 convs per block, translate 2, no cutout, LS 0.1, alternating flip, max-autotune + CUDA graph, 11 epochs). Change only the epoch count, from 11 to 10, and rescale the LR/Lookahead schedule to the new step count so it still anneals fully. Report per-seed accuracy and the per-seed minimum. This measures this net's slope between 10 and 11 epochs: H1.1.4 asks the slope question of the wide net, and this asks it of the incumbent. If I023 (96/256/576) becomes the new tip first, apply the same 1-epoch cut to that tip instead.

Combine near-misses: put block-3 capacity into the resize recipe. E012 suggests block-3 width is the capacity that 100 classes need. E013 and E017 sit 0.1-0.2 pp short, and extra epochs barely help there (E017 gave +0.11 pp/epoch). Start from E013 (commit b0eba3b: 128/256/576, 11 epochs, first 50% of steps at 24 px via bilinear antialias=True, translate 2, both shapes compiled and graphed in build; 0.7510 at 6.32 s). Change only block-3 width, from 576 to 704 (3 convs per block, head input widened to match). Block 3 runs at 8x8 (4x4 or 6x6 maps during the 24 px phase), so per-image conv MACs rise only ~0.2 G (~+15%).

Exploit throughput at equal math. On E012, move the Nesterov SGD + Lookahead update into compiled torch._foreach_* ops inside the CUDA-graph-captured train step. Read the per-step LR and Lookahead alpha from a precomputed GPU tensor table indexed by a GPU step counter, so there is no Python-side scalar update per step. Capture in build on synthetic data; prepare must still reset the parameters, the momentum buffers, the Lookahead slow weights and the step counter. The numerics must match the current update (verify the parameter delta in a short synthetic check).

Free fixed-cost cleanup. On E012, in build, allocate and H2D-copy synthetic uint8 tensors of the exact real dataset shape ([50000,32,32,3] images, [50000] labels) through the same code path prepare uses (pinned staging, .cuda(), permute/normalize kernels), then free them. No real data is touched in build.

Follow-up to E015, which showed the regime is sample-limited, not step-limited: going from batch 1024 to 768 left accuracy flat and cost +5% time. Test whether a larger batch buys throughput. On E012 (11 epochs, translate 2), change only the batch size, from 1024 to 1536. Keep the per-example LR and wd as airbench defines them (per-step LR x1.5), tie the schedule to the new step count, recapture the CUDA graph for the new shape in build, and handle the last partial batch the same way as now.

One decisive optimizer check. On E012 (11 epochs, translate 2), replace Nesterov SGD on the block conv filters (not the whitening layer, BN or head) with Muon in the airbench94_muon form: Newton-Schulz orthogonalized momentum, lr ~0.24, momentum 0.6, nesterov. BN, biases and head stay on the current SGD with the current schedule. Lookahead stays as it is. Run Newton-Schulz in bf16 inside the compiled step and capture it in build. Prepare must reset the Muon momentum buffers.

Exploit: make Muon cheap at equal math. Start from E025 (commit 50d39d6: E024 tip plus Muon on the block conv filters, lr ~0.24, momentum 0.6, nesterov; 0.7622 at 7.26 s). Change only how the Muon update is implemented, not what it computes. (a) Group the same-shape conv filters (block-2 conv2/conv3, block-3 conv2/conv3, and any others that match) and run Newton-Schulz on each stacked group as one batched bf16 bmm. (b) Put the whole Muon step (momentum update, nesterov blend, NS, renorm, param update) into the same compiled function as the fused foreach SGD+Lookahead update, inside the CUDA-graph-captured train step. Read the LR from the GPU step table. Momentum buffers stay persistent, are captured in build on synthetic data, and are zeroed in prepare. Check in a short synthetic test that the parameter delta matches E025's per-parameter loop to bf16 tolerance.

Exploit: spend Muon's accuracy gain on epochs. Start from the I032 result if it was kept as the Muon base, otherwise from E025 (commit 50d39d6). Change only the epoch count, from 11 to 9.5. Rescale the LR, Lookahead and Muon schedules to the new step count so they still anneal fully, and keep the 24 px phase at the first 50% of steps. Report per-seed accuracy. If the 3-seed mean margin over 0.753 is under 0.3 pp, rerun once and pool before promoting it (H1.1.3 rule).

Exploit throughput along the batch axis. On the tip E024 (128/256/704, 50% of steps at 24 px with antialias, translate 2, LS 0.1, alternating flip, batch 1536, fused foreach SGD+Lookahead, 11 epochs), change only the batch size, from 1536 to 2048. Hold the per-example LR and wd fixed (per-step LR x4/3), tie the warmup/decay and Lookahead schedule to the new step count, recapture the CUDA graphs for both resolutions in build, and handle the last partial batch the same way as now.

Exploit: spend Muon's margin on resize, the cheapest accuracy-for-time lever. Resize costs ~0.4 pp/s (E008/E013/E018); cutting epochs costs ~0.75 pp/s (E020). Start from the I032 result if it was kept as the fused-Muon base, otherwise from E025 (commit 50d39d6: E024 tip plus Muon on the block conv filters, lr 0.24, momentum 0.6, 11 ep, batch 1536). Change only the 24 px fraction, from the first 50% of steps to the first 75% (bilinear antialias=True after flip and translate, LR/Lookahead/Muon schedules still tied to step count). Both shapes stay compiled and graphed in build, with no recompile in timed train. Report per-seed accuracy. This is the head-to-head alternative to I033 (epoch cut) for spending the same margin; if both run, compare pp lost per second saved.

Explore the Muon x augmentation interaction (D007: C0074/C0075/C0077 report that Muon gains more than baseline optimizers from stronger augmentation, and that weak augmentation causes late spectral collapse). H4.1's 'weaker regularization is better at ~10 ep' was learned under SGD (E004, E011). Start from the I032 Muon base (or E025 if I032 is not kept). Change only the translate amplitude, from 2 px back to 4 px, in both resolution phases. Everything else stays fixed.

Exploit: spend the tip's margin on epochs. Start from tip E028 (commit 88b116f). First confirm in the code that it is the Muon line: Muon lr 0.24 / momentum 0.6 on block convs, fused into the graphed step, 128/256/704, first 50% of steps at 24 px with antialias, translate 2, LS 0.1, alternating flip, batch 2048, 9.5 ep, fused SGD+Lookahead on the rest. Change only the epoch count, from 9.5 to 8.75. Rescale the LR, Lookahead and Muon schedules to the new step count so they still anneal fully, keep the 24 px phase at the first 50% of steps, and recapture graphs in build if the step count is baked in. Report per-seed accuracy. If the 3-seed margin over 0.753 is under 0.3 pp, rerun once and pool before promoting (H1.1.3 rule). This also measures the Muon slope below 9.5 ep: E027 gave 0.29 pp/ep for 11 to 9.5.

Exploit throughput on the batch axis (E024: 1024 to 1536 gave -3.1%; E028: 1536 to 2048 gave -3.9%, both with accuracy flat). On tip E028, change only the batch size, from 2048 to 3072. Hold the per-example LR and wd fixed for the SGD-trained parameters (per-step LR x1.5). Treat the Muon lr exactly as E028's 1536-to-2048 change did (check the commit and use the same convention). Tie warmup/decay, Lookahead and Muon schedules to the new step count, recapture both resolution graphs in build, and handle the last partial batch the same way as now. Report per-seed accuracy and the total step count (about 155).

Margin builder (rewrite of I041 onto the current tip). Muon lr 0.24 / momentum 0.6 come from airbench94_muon's CIFAR-10 37-to-10-epoch setting at batch 2000. D007 (C0053/C0056/C0065) says shorter horizons favor different step sizes, and Muon tolerates larger lr. On tip E028 (9.5 ep, batch 2048), change only the Muon peak lr, from 0.24 to 0.32: same schedule shape, same momentum, SGD groups unchanged. The precomputed GPU LR table changes; nothing else does.

Crux test: is resize still the cheaper lever now that Muon flattened the epoch curve? Under SGD, resize cost ~0.4 pp/s and epochs ~0.75 pp/s, so resize won. Under Muon, epochs cost ~0.31 pp/s (E027), and resize at 75% cost ~1-1.8 pp/s (E029). The marginal resize rate near 50% under Muon is unmeasured. On tip E028, change only the 24 px fraction, from the first 50% to the first 40% of steps (same antialiased bilinear downsample, schedules tied to step count, both shapes still graphed in build). Report per-seed accuracy.

Explore a schedule component that may be redundant under Muon. airbench94_muon trains without the SGD-era Lookahead, and orthogonalized updates already damp step noise. Lookahead may now only slow late progress at 9.5 ep. On tip E028, change only one thing: remove Lookahead (no slow weights, no _foreach_lerp_ sync) for all parameter groups. Keep the LR/Muon schedules and everything else unchanged, recapture graphs in build, and keep prepare resetting all remaining state.

New Lvl3 under H4.2, from D009 (C0094, C0095, C0099): a zero-cost accuracy-per-step lever. On tip E031, change only the Newton-Schulz polynomial coefficients. Replace the fixed airbench quintic (a, b, c) = (3.4445, -4.7750, 2.0315) with Polar-Express-style per-iteration coefficients at the same iteration count. First confirm the current count in the code; E025's notes suggest 3. Keep the same pre-normalization, including the small safety factor, and keep bf16. Iteration count, momentum, lr, schedule and the stacked bmm grouping stay the same. Verify on a random 704x6336 matrix that the singular values after NS fall in [0.7, 1.2] before running.

Margin builder from E030's implication. Translate 4 hurt more under Muon (-0.62 pp) than under SGD (-0.35 pp), so the weak-augmentation optimum may sit below 2 px under Muon. On tip E031, change only the random-translate amplitude, from 2 px to 1 px (reflect padding as now) in both resolution phases. Everything else is fixed.

Noise floor on the actual tip, required by the H1.1.3 rule because E031's margin is +0.21 pp (< 0.3). Rerun E031 (commit 3797e1a) unchanged, once. Pool it with E031, and use E028 and E034 for context, to estimate the run-to-run sd of a 3-seed mean on the Muon line, where per-trial same-seed nondeterminism was up to 0.9 pp under SGD. Report per-seed accuracy and time.

Follow-up to E035, where removing Lookahead cost -0.81 pp, so averaging is first-order. Test stronger averaging. On tip E031, first read the Lookahead constants in the code (cadence k, peak decay, ramp exponent). Then change only the peak decay of the slow-weight update from 0.95**k to 0.97**k, which roughly doubles the averaging window in steps. Keep the same cubic ramp, cadence and final sync to the slow weights. The GPU alpha table changes; nothing else does.

Close the Muon lr axis from below. E033 showed that 0.32 was worse (-0.33 pp) at 8.75 ep and batch 2048, so the optimum is at or below 0.24. On tip E031, change only the Muon peak lr, from 0.24 to 0.18: same schedule shape, momentum 0.6, SGD groups unchanged. Only the GPU LR table changes.

Zero-cost schedule leftover from 37-epoch runs, re-posed on the Muon tip. At 8.75 ep, whiten_bias_epochs 3 trains the whitening bias for about 34% of the run. On tip E031, first confirm in the code that a whitening-bias phase exists and what its semantics are. If it does not exist, record a no-op and do not run. Otherwise change only whiten_bias_epochs, from 3 to 1 (scaled about 3/37 x 8.75 ≈ 0.7, rounded up).
